events.title: Li Shimin's Xuanwu Gate Ambush
events.description: In Chang'an, Li Shimin, a prince of the Tang dynasty, ambushed his brothers in a palace coup. Afterward he forced his father to name him heir.
events.significance: Li Shimin soon became Emperor Taizong. His reign is often called one of the golden ages of Chinese history.

events.title: Congress Votes for Independence
events.description: The Continental Congress adopted a resolution declaring the American colonies free of Great Britain. The wording of the Declaration of Independence was not approved until two days later.
events.significance: John Adams expected July 2 to be the great American anniversary. The vote was the decisive act that created the United States.

events.title: President Garfield Is Shot
events.description: Charles J. Guiteau shot U.S. President James Garfield at a Washington railroad station. Garfield lingered for weeks and died of infection on September 19.
events.significance: The shooting led to civil service reform in the United States. It also exposed the limits of medical care at the time.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Vanishes Over the Pacific
events.description: Aviator Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan disappeared over the Pacific Ocean. They were attempting the first round-the-world flight along the equator.
events.significance: The disappearance is among the most famous unsolved mysteries of the 20th century. It made Earhart a lasting symbol of daring and adventure.

events.title: Civil Rights Act Becomes Law
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964. The law banned discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin.
events.significance: The act outlawed segregation in public places and discrimination in employment. It was a landmark of the American civil rights movement.
